welcomeMessage: This website is provided as a public service by the Menlo Park Police Department. In an effort to protect victim privacy, this website does not provide information regarding juvenile offenders, or specific information regarding calls for service that are sensitive in nature. The Department does not guarantee the accuracy, completeness or timeliness of the information contained in this website regarding specific incidents, crimes or people with respect to the omission of the information that may have not yet been filed or is pending filing with a court of jurisdiction relating to criminal offenses. With regard to people listed on the arrest page, arrests shown on that page are generated by arrests entered into the Records Management System at the Police Department and do not reflect ALL arrests in the City.
arrestText: Using this website, members of the public will have access to public information regarding individuals arrested by the Menlo Park Police Department. Be advised that during the course of any investigation any offense charges can be changed or updated. Unless otherwise declared "guilty" or "convicted," offenders are considered innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.
crimeStatsDisclaimer: Please be advised that crime statistics are based off the initial crime reported. During an investigation, crimes could be updated and/or changed from the initial report.
stopDataStatsDisclaimer: Demographic information is based on the officer's personal observation and initial observation and initial perception only. This information is not solicited from the person stopped or obtained from the person's driver's license or other identification. The information reported may not reflect the demographic information on the person's identification of how the person identifies.
stopDataStatsDefinitions:
· “Reason for Stop” refers to the primary reason why the officer stopped the person.

o Traffic violation

o Reasonable suspicion that the person was engaged in criminal activity

o Probable cause to arrest or search

o Probable cause to take into custody under Welfare and Institutions Code section 5150

o Known to be on parole/probation/PRCS/mandatory supervision

o Knowledge of outstanding arrest warrant/wanted person

o Investigation to determine whether the person is truant

o Consensual encounter resulting in a search

· “Perceived Race of Ethnicity of Person Stopped” refers to the officer’s perception of the race or ethnicity of the person stopped.When reporting this data element, the officer shall make their determination of the person’s race or ethnicity, or ask or make comments or statements designed to elicit this information.Officers may report one or more of the following options for the person stopped:

o Asian

o Black/African American

o Hispanic/Latine (x)

o Middle Eastern or South Asian

o Native American

o Pacific Islander

o White

· “Perceived Gender of Person Stopped” refers to the officer’s perception to the person’s gender. When reporting this data element, the officer shall make their determination of the person’s gender based on personal observation only. The officer shall not ask the person stopped their gender or use the gender specified on the person’s driver’s license or other identification, recognizing that the officer’s observation may not reflect the gender specified on the person’s identification

o Cisgender man/boy

o Cisgender woman/girl

o Transgender man/boy

o Transgender woman/girl

o Nonbinary

· “Perceived or Known Disability of Person Stopped” refers to the officer’s perception that the person stopped displayed signs of one or more of the following conditions; the officer’s knowledge that the person stopped has one or more of the following conditions because the person stopped so advised the officer or the officer’s prior knowledge that the person stopped had one or more of the following conditions.

o Deafness or difficulty hearing

o Speech impairment or limited use of language

o Blind or limited vision

o Mental health condition

o Intellectual or developmental disability, including dementia

o None

· “Actions Taken During Stop” refers to (more than one can be selected)

o Asked for consent to search person

o Asked for consent to search property

o Asked for identification of stopped persons passenger

o Asked whether the person is on parole, probation, PRCS, or some other form of mandatory supervision

o Canine used to search for, locate, and/or detect contraband

o Curbside detention

o Field sobriety test conducted

o Frisk/pat search of the persons outer clothing was conducted

o None

o Patrol car detention

o Person photographed

o Person removed from vehicle by order

o Property was seized

o Ran name of stopped persons passenger

o Search of person was conducted

o Search of property was conducted

o Vehicle impounded

o Baton or other impact weapon drawn

o Baton or other impact weapon used

o Chemical spray used

o Electronic control device pointed at person or sparked

o Electronic control device used in dart-mode

o Electronic control device used in drive-stun mode

o Firearm discharged

o Firearm pointed as person

o Firearm unholstered

o Handcuffed or flex cuffed

o Impact projectile discharged or used

o Impact projectile weapon pointed at person

o Officer’s canine bit or held person

o Officer’s canine removed from vehicle or used to search

o Person removed from vehicle by physical contact

o Physical compliance tactics and techniques

o Use of vehicle in apprehension of stopped person

· “Search Rates” refers to stops with actions “Search of person was conducted” and “Search of property was conducted” for each perceived gender

· “Discovery Rates” refers to stops with evidence discovered (except “None”) for each perceived gender

· “Result of Stop” refers to the outcome of the stop

o No action

o Verbal warning

o Written warning

o Citation for infraction

o In-field cite and release

o Custodial arrest pursuant to outstanding warrant

o Custodial arrest without warrant

o Field interview card completed

o Noncriminal transport or caretaking transport. This includes transport by an officer, transport by ambulance, or transport by another agency.

o Contacted parent/legal guardian or other person legally responsible for the person.

o Psychiatric hold (pursuant to Welfare & Institutions Code sections 5150 and/or 5585.20)

o Contacted U.S Department of Homeland Security (e.g., Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border Protection)
